evidence.detail: The constructor builds an array of rs/l/F Sprite frames from an arbitrary base name by loading baseName + frameIndex for each frame, or accepts a caller-supplied Sprite[] directly.
The class stores a frame interval in milliseconds, advances the current frame when System.currentTimeMillis passes the next-frame deadline, and wraps back to frame 0 at the end of the array.

Three public draw wrappers all fetch the current animated frame and delegate to distinct Sprite draw methods, proving the object is a reusable animated sprite sequence rather than a one-off resource holder.
Exact v308 initializes the shared singleton with base name 'glitter', 4 frames and a 100 ms interval, providing a concrete live use without constraining the generic class role.
